$description: Dark mode. Same token contract as light, re-pointed at the dark end of each ramp. A new theme must provide every token listed in light.tokens.json. Translucent roles carry the same alpha extension mechanism as light: the dark glass is the pack's own tint at a low alpha over the near-black ground, because in dark the thickness reads through what the pane adds, not what it hides.

card.$description: The resting surface as dark glass: a breath of the pack's tint over the ground, compositing to a step the ground does not have, with the rim and hairline carrying the edge. Contrast pairs composite it over the page ground.

popover.$description: The floating surface, the thickest pane in the ladder: nearly opaque in dark, because it overlaps text a reader is reading, and thickness is how the ladder says closer.

sidebar.$description: Sidebar surface, the thinnest pane in the ladder: the faintest of the three dark glasses, holding the ground long enough to carry navigation.

elevation-rim.$description: The glass edge finish in dark: a faint light along a pane's top rim. Far fainter than light mode, because a hot highlight on a dark ground reads as a glow, and a glow is the one thing this finish is not.

elevation-inner.$description: The inside hairline in dark, barely there: thickness in dark is a suggestion the rim and the shade make together.

elevation-contact.$description: The tight shadow where a lifted pane meets its ground. Darker and heavier than light mode, because depth in dark comes from what the pane blocks.

elevation-shade.$description: The wide, soft ambient shadow under a lifted pane in dark.
